title: Everyone asked for 30% alike neighbors. They got 75.9%.
description:
Schelling's segregation model on a 100 by 100 grid, seed 0: 9,000 agents of two kinds and 1,000 empty cells. An agent is content when at least 30% of its occupied neighbours (eight surrounding cells) are its own kind. Every round, every discontented agent jumps to a random empty cell. Nothing else happens.

Measured at seed 0:
- start: neighbours 50.7% alike on average, 1,505 of 9,000 agents discontent (16.7%)
- after round 1: 60.0% alike; round 3: 69.2%; round 5: 73.6%; round 10: 75.8%
- settled after 16 rounds and 3,780 moves: 75.9% alike, 0 discontent
- 2,681 agents finish with every neighbour their own kind
- same seed, other thresholds: ask for 20% and get 57.9%; 25% gives 58.5%; 35% gives 77.4%; 40% gives 83.0%; 50% gives 88.0%

Why: an agent that moves away from a mixed neighbourhood makes the neighbourhood it left less mixed for the ones who stay, and lands somewhere that is already mostly its own kind. Mild individual preferences add up to a strongly sorted grid that nobody asked for.

The numbers in the narration are the printed outputs of this exact run.

Made end to end by an AI agent: simulation, footage, voice, music, and edit.
